title: How much does paint protection film cost in Surrey?
author: Paul Dalton
excerpt: Compare Miracle Detail’s VAT-inclusive PPF starting prices in Lingfield, Surrey. See which panels each package covers and what changes your quote.

cover.alt: White Honda Civic Type R in the Miracle Detail studio, Lingfield, after full-panel paint protection film

body:
At Miracle Detail in Lingfield, full-front [paint protection film](/paint-protection-film-ppf/) starts at £1,800 including VAT. The Track Pack starts at £2,400 and full-car coverage starts at £4,800, also including VAT. The first decision is which parts of your car you want to protect. For someone who puts most of their miles on the M25, the answer may be written across the bonnet of the car they already own.

## What does £1,800 of full-front PPF cover?

![Front of a white Honda Civic Type R with paint protection film in the Miracle Detail studio, Lingfield, Surrey](media/miracle/m0iumy4zkxa7.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "The white Civic Type R in the studio. Its film covers every panel, the front included.")

Imagine walking around the nose of the car with a roll of masking tape to mark every panel on the estimate. At Miracle Detail you would mark the entire bonnet, both front wings and the front bumper. You would also mark the headlamps and fog lights where fitted, the mirror caps and faces, the A-pillars and the leading edge of the roof. There is quite a difference between that list and a strip of film across the first few inches of a bonnet.

A full bonnet also changes where the film ends. If you have previously owned a car with a partial bonnet kit, you may remember seeing a line across the panel after a wash. Ask Paul to walk you around the studio’s [coverage illustration](/paint-protection-film-ppf/) and point out where each piece ends on your particular model. A diagram is especially helpful on a car with a contrasting roof, exposed carbon or a complicated front bumper.

## When is the Track Pack worth the extra £600?

The extra coverage is along the sills, the low sections running beneath the doors. Look behind the front wheels of your current car. If that paint carries far more peppering than the doors above it, you have a practical reason to ask about sill coverage on the next one. You can make that judgement even if the car will never see a circuit.

At the published starting prices, adding the sills takes the total from £1,800 to £2,400 including VAT. Ask for the difference on your own car before deciding. If you are choosing between sill coverage and an unrelated cosmetic extra, think about which surface you are already paying to touch up or which damage on your previous car bothered you enough to notice every time you washed it.

## What changes with a full-car installation?

![Hands smoothing wet film onto the rear wing of a white Honda Civic Type R with a red squeegee](media/miracle/0tiws7c8yjlu.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1400 "Film being squeegeed onto the Civic Type R's rear wing.")

Full-car PPF brings the remaining painted bodywork into the job, including the doors, rear bumper, boot lid and the rest of the roof. The studio lists mirrors and lights too. The word “full” is worth discussing if the car has painted aero parts, aftermarket extensions or unusual trim. Have any particularly important pieces named on the estimate so that you can recognise the scope when you collect the vehicle.

The [white Honda Civic Type R](/car-detail-gallery/?job=honda-civic-type-r-white) in Miracle Detail’s gallery illustrates the choice. It came from the dealership for film on every panel. Its owner also commissioned underside protection and work on the wheels and glass. Those details make the gallery a useful reference when discussing a similar car. They also explain why a photograph of a completed project cannot tell you the price of its film installation.

## Why can two cars get different quotes?

![Clear film laid wet over the rear wing and tailgate of a white Honda Civic Type R before fitting](media/miracle/u9890lumjlno.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "Fresh film over the Civic's rear wing and tailgate, before it is worked into place.")

Coverage tells you where the film goes. Condition helps determine what needs doing before it goes on. A bonnet with visible scratches or old touch-ups calls for a different conversation from one delivered with sound paint. Clear film leaves the underlying colour visible. Point out existing chips, any repainting and any areas with previous film before agreeing a finish. That gives the installer a chance to explain what you are likely to see afterwards.

Shape matters as well. A wide, simple painted panel presents a different fitting problem from a bumper broken up by air intakes and tight returns. Ask where edges can be tucked on your model, where a join may be visible and whether anything needs removing. These are useful questions about the finished installation, even for an owner who has no interest in the fitting process itself.

## Is it worth covering a car you already own?

Start with the years ahead. If you enjoy the car, plan to keep it and dislike the steady accumulation of fresh chips, it may make sense to protect sound areas while accepting a few existing marks. If the front bumper already needs paint, have it assessed before buying film. Where refinishing is involved, the bodyshop and installer can advise on timing for that particular paint system.

There is a different calculation for a satin or matte finish. An owner may care as much about keeping the appearance consistent across adjacent panels as about the number of chips. Ask to see the proposed film finish alongside the car in daylight. Miracle Detail’s Journal has a [dedicated guide to matte and satin paint](/why-matte-and-satin-paint-needs-ppf/) for owners weighing that decision.

## How should you compare two Surrey PPF estimates?

Put both panel lists next to one another. Check the bonnet coverage, sills, lights, roof edge, preparation, VAT-inclusive total and any aftercare or inspection arrangements. Clarify what would happen if just one panel of film needed replacing later. Two totals that look several hundred pounds apart may describe different work. Once the scope is clear, the comparison becomes much easier.

One useful way to narrow the choice is to mark your three priorities on a photograph before you ask for prices. A driver might circle the bonnet, the area ahead of the rear wheels and the edge of the boot where luggage passes over it. Those marks give Paul a starting point for a bespoke discussion if the standard packages leave one priority uncovered. Bring that photograph to the appointment for reference.

For a quote from Lingfield, send Paul the make, model, year and finish, plus a front three-quarter photograph and a close-up of any area you are concerned about. Mention whether you want full-front, Track Pack or full-car pricing, and say if you would like two options side by side. Appointments are at Miracle Detail, Unit 10, Jesmor Trading Estate, St Piers Lane, Lingfield, Surrey RH7 6PN.

title: PPF or ceramic coating for a new car? How to choose in Surrey
author: Paul Dalton
excerpt: Choosing protection for a new car in Surrey? Compare stone-chip protection, easier washing and combined coverage using two real Lingfield studio projects.

cover.alt: Blue Porsche Macan Turbo in the Miracle Detail studio after paint correction and Feynlab ceramic coating

body:
Choose [paint protection film](/paint-protection-film-ppf/) if your main concern is stone chips on exposed paint. Choose a [ceramic coating](/ceramic-coatings/) if you want easier washing and a gloss finish that is easier to maintain. Consider both if those priorities apply to different parts of the same car. A motorway commuter who is tired of touching in the bonnet and an owner who spends Sunday morning washing a garaged car can sensibly make different decisions about the same model.

## What problem are you trying to solve?

Think about the last car you sold. Perhaps the front looked tired after three winters, although the doors still cleaned up beautifully. Perhaps the nose was fine, but washing a large estate took up most of an afternoon. Write down the one thing you would change about that experience. It is a better starting point for a new-car consultation than the name of a product someone else chose.

Film and coating work in different ways. PPF puts a replaceable physical layer over selected panels. A ceramic coating changes how the treated surface behaves when it gets wet or dirty. Both can preserve an attractive finish, but only film gives the stone something substantial to strike before it reaches the paint. Even film has limits. A hard impact can mark the panel underneath or leave damage in the film that requires replacement.

## For the driver who covers motorway miles

![Front wing, wheel and bumper corner of a white Honda Civic Type R covered in paint protection film](media/miracle/88d4v5y8pg7h.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "The Civic Type R's front wing and bumper corner, under full-panel film.")

If the car frequently joins fast traffic, pay attention to the leading surfaces. The front bumper, bonnet, wings and mirror caps are sensible places to begin the discussion. At the Lingfield studio, the [full-front package](/paint-protection-film-ppf/) also takes in the A-pillars and leading roof edge. If the sills on your old car picked up grit thrown by the front wheels, look at the extra coverage in the Track Pack.

A driver travelling from Oxted with a fixed protection budget might put the money into the front of the car and continue washing the remaining paint as usual. There is no need to make one product decision for every surface. Ask for the coverage drawing and look at it from the side as well as the front. The point where protection ends matters as much as the list of parts included.

## For the owner who enjoys a freshly washed car

![Front of a blue Porsche Macan Turbo under hexagon lights in the Miracle Detail studio in Lingfield](media/miracle/bhuk96a2ks9o.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "The Macan Turbo arrived new with swirls. It was corrected, then given a Feynlab ceramic coating.")

A ceramic coating is worth considering if your priority is how the paint cleans, dries and looks between washes. Water behaviour is the change you are most likely to notice first. The car still gets dirty, particularly around the tailgate and lower doors, but the routine for keeping on top of it can become easier. A coating also makes most sense if you can follow the maintenance advice supplied with it.

Take the [blue Porsche Macan Turbo](/car-detail-gallery/?job=porsche-macan-turbo-blue) in Miracle Detail’s project archive. The studio records that the car arrived new with swirls and scratches. It received paint correction followed by a Feynlab ceramic coating. The glass received its own treatment. The order matters. Polishing addressed the visible marks. Coating preserved the prepared finish. If your goal is a sharp reflection in dark paint, ask the installer to explain both parts of that job.

## When does a combination make sense?

![Close-up of the blue metallic paint on a Porsche Macan Turbo reflecting a studio light](media/miracle/bi3jospb0lvp.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1400 "The Macan's blue metallic paint, close up under the studio lights.")

Picture a daily-driven performance estate. Its owner wants impact protection on the nose, likes washing the car at home and wants consistent water behaviour along the doors. Front-end film and a compatible coating on the exposed paint could address both priorities. If coating over the film is also proposed, ask which product the film manufacturer supports and what that means for aftercare. Have each treated surface identified on the estimate.

Another owner might take the approach seen on the studio’s [white Honda Civic Type R](/car-detail-gallery/?job=honda-civic-type-r-white). That car came directly from its supplying dealer and received full-panel film. The brief also covered other areas of the vehicle. It illustrates how far new-car protection can extend when the owner wants broad coverage. Use the project photographs to pick out the parts that matter to you rather than assuming every item belongs on your own order.

## What about dealer-applied protection?

Ask the dealer for the name of anything already applied and where it was used. “Paint protection included” can describe several things. The studio can give more useful preparation advice with the product details in hand. If the car is still on order, ask what cosmetic preparation the dealer plans to carry out and agree your preferences before collection. Keep a copy of the handover paperwork alongside your protection estimate.

When you collect, take a few photographs outside and look along the bonnet and doors as well as straight at them. If you see a chip or scratch, record it and raise it with the supplying dealer while the handover is fresh. Send the studio the photographs ahead of your appointment. A phone image can start a discussion, even when the final decision depends on seeing clean paint under suitable light.

## A straightforward way to choose

Ask for the estimate to be written around how you use the car. For motorway mileage, lead with the panels you want protected from chips. For easier maintenance, lead with the finish, parking arrangements and how the car is washed. For a combined installation, ask which areas receive film, which receive coating and how to look after both. This gives you a practical comparison even when the available packages carry unfamiliar names.

Ask how collection will work if your chosen treatments are applied in sequence. Knowing when the vehicle can be driven home and when it can first be washed helps you plan around a handover, a commute or a long journey. Keep the instructions handy.

If you are [collecting a new car](/new-car-detail-protection/) in Surrey, contact Paul at Miracle Detail in Lingfield with the model, finish and expected handover date. Include one sentence about what bothered you most on the previous car. “The bonnet was peppered by 20,000 miles” tells an installer more about the right starting point than a request for the most expensive package on the list.

title: How much does ceramic coating cost in Surrey, and what is included?
author: Paul Dalton
excerpt: Professional ceramic coating starts at £540 including VAT at Miracle Detail in Lingfield. See how preparation, coating choice and treated surfaces affect the quote.

cover.alt: Red Audi Q8 in the Miracle Detail studio after three-stage paint correction and a five-year ceramic coating

body:
Professional [ceramic coating](/ceramic-coatings/) at Miracle Detail in Lingfield starts at £540 including VAT (£450 before VAT). That figure is a [starting price for this studio](/car-detailing-studio/). Your written quote should identify the coating, the paint preparation, the surfaces included and the final amount payable. Of those four details, preparation is often the hardest to judge from home, especially if the car looks immaculate until the sun catches the bonnet.

## What does the starting price tell you?

It gives you a figure against which to plan a conversation. It does not tell you that a particular coating, a [two-stage polish](/journal/new-car-paint-correction-before-ceramic-coating/) or a set of wheels is included on your car. Ask Paul to identify the entry option appropriate to your vehicle and to price any additional work separately. If the figure changes after inspection, you should be able to point to the reason on the estimate.

Imagine comparing two proposals for a black estate. One includes application to the painted panels after routine preparation. The other includes several hours refining visible wash marks and a separate treatment for the glass. Reading just the totals tells you very little. Reading the scope lets you decide whether you actually want the refinement and the glass treatment, and what each is worth to you.

## Where does preparation end and correction begin?

![Red Audi Q8 paint before and after machine polishing, with the swirl marks gone on the right](media/miracle/x79s2tem0wrz.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x788 "Swirl marks on the Q8's red paint, before and after correction.")

A coating needs a properly prepared surface. Washing and removing bonded contamination deal with material sitting on the paint. Polishing deals with imperfections in the finish itself. You may feel one as roughness when the car is clean and see the other as a fine halo around a reflection. They are different jobs. A quotation that simply says “full preparation” is worth a follow-up question.

Ask the studio to show you a representative area once the car is clean. A patch of bonnet under a concentrated light can make the decision easier than a long description over the phone. If you are comfortable with a few minor marks, say so. If the whole purpose of the booking is to improve the appearance of dark paint, explain that before selecting a coating by the number of years on its label.

## Which Feynlab coating are you paying for?

![Bottle of Feynlab Ultra V3 ceramic coating held up beside a red Audi Q8 in the studio](media/miracle/vmv2o20lxve1.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1400 "Feynlab Ultra V3, photographed beside the Audi Q8.")

[Miracle Detail’s range](/ceramic-coatings/) includes Feynlab Original Ceramic, listed at one to two years, and the three-year Ceramic by Paul Dalton, developed with Feynlab. The range also includes two five-year options, Heal Lite and Ultra V2. Seeing two products with the same stated duration is a clue that longevity alone will not settle the choice. Ask which properties you would actually notice on your own vehicle.

For instance, the studio describes Heal Lite as offering a heat-assisted response to minor surface marks. Ultra V2 is another five-year choice with a different formulation. An owner who parks outside, an enthusiast who hand washes every week and someone planning to change cars next year may value those features differently. Ask what conditions apply to the stated durability and which ongoing care the installer recommends for the specific product.

## Are wheels, glass and trim included?

![Gloss black pillar trim on a red Audi Q8, scratched on the left and polished on the right](media/miracle/1yyyjftv439l.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x885 "The Q8's gloss-black trim, before (left) and after (right).")

Think in terms of surfaces. Paint, exterior glass, wheel faces and the backs of wheels are separate items that can require different access and products. If brake dust is your biggest frustration, ask precisely which wheel surfaces the price covers. If visibility in wet weather is a priority, ask about a glass treatment and how it should be maintained. Put any chosen extras on the written quote.

The studio’s [Audi Q8 project](/car-detail-gallery/?job=audi-q8-red) shows why this distinction matters. The gallery describes a car with around 4,000 miles that received extensive three-stage correction and a five-year ceramic treatment. Its windows were treated and the wheels were removed and protected inside and out. That is a useful example of a substantial brief. A starting price for ceramic coating cannot be used to reconstruct the invoice for that Audi.

## How do you judge value over time?

Count the things you will still have to do. You will still wash the car, dry it carefully and deal promptly with contamination. If you use a regular wash service, find out whether it can follow the recommended routine. If you wash at home, ask which products you can keep using. A treatment fits your budget better when its maintenance fits the time and facilities you already have.

Also consider the problem you are paying to solve. A buyer disappointed by chips on a previous car should compare the price of film on the vulnerable panels before committing the whole budget to coating. An owner delighted with the existing paint who mostly wants quicker maintenance may prefer to spend on coating and aftercare. Both decisions start with an honest account of how the car will be driven and cleaned.

## What should a written estimate say?

Look for the product name, the expected preparation, the extent of any polishing, the surfaces treated, the collection arrangements and the VAT-inclusive total. Ask when the first wash can take place, what to do if it rains soon after collection and who to contact with an aftercare question. Specific advice from the installer is more useful than applying a timetable you found for a different coating online.

Think about collection day as part of the purchase. Ask to see the car in the light before you leave and keep the product name, treatment date and written care instructions together. If a panel is refinished later, that record gives the bodyshop and detailer a useful reference when deciding what needs to be reapplied and how to bring the repaired area back into line with the surrounding finish. That record also helps when the vehicle changes hands.

For a Surrey quotation, send Miracle Detail the year, model, colour and a photograph taken in daylight. Include any history of respraying, previous coatings or repeated automatic washes. Tell Paul if you would like an entry option alongside a longer-duration alternative with the same preparation. With the paintwork and surfaces held constant, you can see what the change in coating actually adds to the cost.

title: Does a brand-new car need paint correction before ceramic coating?
author: Paul Dalton
excerpt: Does new paint need polishing before coating? See how finish, visible defects and a BMW M3 Touring project informed the decision at Miracle Detail in Surrey.

cover.alt: Black BMW M3 Touring in the Miracle Detail studio after two-stage paint correction and Feynlab ceramic coating

body:
Sometimes. A brand-new car needs an inspection before ceramic coating, and the condition of the paint determines whether it needs [machine polishing](/paint-correction-and-polishing/). Sound gloss paint may require only cleaning and the preparation specified for the chosen coating. Visible swirls or haze may justify refinement. A new registration tells you the age of the vehicle. It tells you little about the finish on the bonnet under a bright light.

## How can a new car already have swirl marks?

Paint can be handled several times between manufacture and handover. A car may be stored, moved, cleaned for display and prepared again for collection. Fine marks can become visible when a point of light reflects off the surface. Their presence alone cannot tell you exactly when they were introduced. What matters at collection is recording the condition while you and the supplying dealer can look at it together.

Walk around the car in daylight if possible. Look along the doors from a shallow angle, then move your head while looking at a reflection in the bonnet. A mark that disappears when you change position may return as soon as the light catches it again. Photograph anything that concerns you from a little distance as well as close up, so that someone else can find the same area later.

## What happened with the BMW M3 Touring in Lingfield?

![Rear three-quarter view of a black BMW M3 Touring in the Miracle Detail studio in Lingfield](media/miracle/mfebt050hmjw.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "The new M3 Touring in the studio. It had a two-stage correction and a five-year Feynlab coating.")

Miracle Detail’s project archive records a new [BMW M3 Touring](/car-detail-gallery/?job=bmw-m3-touring) brought directly to the studio. Paul carried out a two-stage paint correction to address swirls and scratches, followed by a five-year Feynlab [ceramic coating](/ceramic-coatings/). The glass was also polished and given a water-repellent treatment. The car’s delivery condition made correction relevant even though its owner had barely begun to use it.

There are two decisions inside that short account. The first concerns appearance: how much improvement do the visible defects warrant? The second concerns protection: once the surface looks right, what will help the owner maintain it? Keeping those decisions separate lets you discuss each on its merits. The work specified for the BMW provides a real example of the sequence, without prescribing the same process for your own new car.

## What does a proper assessment look for?

![Bonnet of a new black BMW M3 Touring with masking tape on the paint during paint correction](media/miracle/bddz0oxvw4rb.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1050 "Masking tape on the M3 Touring's bonnet during its correction.")

Start with clean paint. Dirt can obscure a scratch, and something that looks like a blemish can turn out to be residue. An inspection can distinguish contamination on top of the surface from defects within the finish. It can also identify places that deserve different treatment, including sharp edges, unusual materials, previous repairs or a factory satin panel on an otherwise glossy car.

Ask Paul to show you the most representative defect and the most difficult one. They may be quite different. A light pattern across a bonnet could respond to gentle refinement, while one isolated scratch might still be visible afterwards. Agreeing which of those outcomes matters to you is useful before anyone proposes a stage count. A small, discreet test area on suitable gloss paint can help establish what improvement is realistic.

## One stage, two stages or no polishing?

![Machine polishing the bonnet of a black BMW M3 Touring in the studio under hexagon lights](media/miracle/v4auo9xj5bck.webp?w=480,800,1086&size=1086x1086 "Machine polishing the M3 Touring's bonnet.")

A single polishing stage may suit light marks when the combination of pad, polish and technique gives an acceptable finish. Two stages generally allow a more corrective pass to be followed by finer finishing. The number describes a method of work. It cannot, by itself, promise how much a scratch will improve or tell you whether a car needs that treatment across every panel.

Clear coat is finite. If there is little visible benefit to further abrasion, preserving the finish can be a sensible choice. A conspicuous isolated defect on a new vehicle may also deserve a conversation with the supplying dealer before a detailer changes it. Factory matte and satin finishes need their own assessment because conventional polishing can alter the sheen. Always identify the finish before agreeing to polish a marked area.

## Will the coating hide what is underneath?

Ceramic coating is applied after the appearance of the paint has been agreed. Do not budget for it as a way of removing swirls. If a mark catches your eye while the car is clean and dry, point it out before application and ask what it is likely to look like afterwards. The moment to agree whether it matters is while preparation choices are still open.

The [blue Porsche Macan Turbo](/car-detail-gallery/?job=porsche-macan-turbo-blue) in the studio gallery offers a second new-car example. Its recorded work included correction for swirls and scratches before ceramic protection. For a buyer weighing the extra cost, these projects are useful conversation starters. Ask to see the type of defect involved and compare it with what you actually see on your own car, preferably under similar lighting.

## What should you agree before delivery day?

If you know the car is [coming to a detailer](/new-car-detail-protection/), speak to the dealer in advance about cosmetic preparation, optional coatings and presentation for handover. Ask what has already been applied. Keep any product information and record existing damage at collection. Avoid rubbing a dusty panel to check a suspected mark. A photograph and a clean inspection at the studio are better ways to resolve the question.

If collection day is overcast, revisit the same panels in clearer light before deciding whether a mark has disappeared. Keep any comparison photographs in pairs, with the camera aimed at the same area from roughly the same angle. Broad photographs show the position on the vehicle, while closer views show the character of the mark. That small amount of context can save an unproductive exchange of tightly cropped images. This is particularly helpful for metallic colours that change appearance as you move around them.

For an appointment in Lingfield, send Paul the model, colour, paint finish and expected collection date. Tell him whether your priority is keeping original paint as untouched as practical or correcting visible defects before coating. Ask for the recommended preparation and any optional correction to be itemised. The result should be a decision you can recognise on the car itself, supported by what you saw together at the studio.

title: Is dry ice cleaning worth it for a classic car underbody? Lessons from a BMW E30 M3
author: Paul Dalton
excerpt: Explore classic car underbody cleaning through a BMW E30 M3 project in Lingfield. See what dry ice can reveal, what it costs per hour and when to pause.

cover.alt: Silver BMW E30 M3 in the Miracle Detail studio during its three-week concours detail

body:
Dry ice cleaning is worth considering when a classic car owner wants to see and document what survives beneath years of grime. Its value depends on what is uncovered and which original finishes can be preserved. At Miracle Detail in Lingfield, [dry ice cleaning](/dry-ice-blasting-and-laser-cleaning/) is listed at £240 per hour including VAT. Before committing to a complete underside, agree which areas matter, how their condition will be assessed and what happens if the cleaning reveals a repair.

## What does dry ice cleaning actually do?

![Dry ice pellets giving off vapour, ready for cleaning the underside of a classic BMW E30 M3](media/miracle/6590pc23c452.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1400 "Dry ice pellets used on the E30 M3's underside.")

In specialist dry ice cleaning, solid carbon dioxide particles are directed at a surface to dislodge contamination. The particles change into gas. There is no spent abrasive grit from the dry ice itself, although the dirt removed from the vehicle still has to be collected. Access, the condition of the underlying finish and the choice of treatment matter as much as the name of the process.

Think of the underside as a collection of different surfaces. A painted floorpan, a textured factory coating, a metal suspension arm and a previously repaired seam may all be within a few inches of each other. A sensible brief identifies what the owner wants revealed and what should be left in place. “Make everything look new” leaves important decisions unanswered on a car whose original finishes are part of its appeal.

## What does the BMW E30 M3 tell us?

![Underside panel of a silver BMW E30 M3 before and after cleaning, with the dirt removed on the right](media/miracle/9f366ibuwufe.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x933 "The E30 M3's underside, before and after cleaning.")

Miracle Detail documents a [silver BMW E30 M3](/car-detail-gallery/?job=bmw-e30-m3-silver) that underwent a three-week concours detail. Its underside was dry ice cleaned and subsequently protected with a [Feynlab industrial coating](/underside-coating/). The wider project included paint correction, leather restoration and dent removal. In the gallery, the underside belongs to a much larger story about bringing an entire car to a standard its owner wanted.

Those three weeks describe the whole commission. They cannot be multiplied by the hourly dry ice rate to estimate the cost of cleaning another BMW. What the example does establish is the sequence: clean the underside, assess the surface that is now visible and decide on appropriate protection. A customer interested only in recording the condition of a recently acquired classic might reasonably stop after inspection and photography.

## When is preserving an original finish the priority?

![BMW E30 M3 underside panel part-way through cleaning, with half still covered in old dirt](media/miracle/cn3d4uq5tllf.webp?w=480,800,1200,1400&size=1400x1400 "Part-way through: half of this panel cleaned, half still to go.")

Suppose your classic still has sections of recognisable factory coating. A uniform black finish might look tidy in an advertisement, yet tell the next person inspecting the car very little about what lies underneath. If originality matters, ask the studio to photograph representative areas before work begins and record where coatings, labels or markings appear vulnerable. Decide together which features deserve to be retained.

A test area gives that discussion something concrete. Look at the boundary between cleaned and untouched material, the texture of the exposed surface and the condition of any seam nearby. A result that looks attractive on one section of the floorpan does not settle what should happen elsewhere. On an older car, components replaced at different times can have very different finishes and histories.

## Will it remove rust or replace a repair?

Cleaning can uncover corrosion that grime or loose material had obscured. It cannot put metal back into a corroded panel, restore a failed seam or confirm the structural condition of the entire car. If a suspect area appears, agree that the studio will document it and discuss the next step before covering it. An appropriate repair assessment may then be more valuable than further cosmetic work.

The same applies to leaks. Cleaning around a component can make it easier to tell where fresh residue returns, but the source still needs diagnosing. If the classic is already booked for mechanical work, tell the studio what your specialist needs to see. A clearly photographed area before dismantling may be more useful than spending the available budget on parts that are about to come off.

## How do you budget for hourly cleaning?

Start with the question you want answered. A new owner may want a documented view of particular arches and suspension areas. Someone presenting a car at an event may want the entire visible underside addressed. Ask for an estimated number of hours for the agreed scope, what access is assumed and how Paul will contact you if the condition changes that estimate.

At the published hourly rate, four hours of cleaning would be £960 including VAT. That is an arithmetic example, not a time estimate for an E30 or any other vehicle. Ask separately about access work, protection and any other treatments. A staged brief with a review point can be helpful if the underside has never been documented or carries a mixture of old finishes.

## Should the underside be coated afterwards?

That depends on what is exposed, how the car will be stored and how often it goes out in poor weather. A regularly driven classic and one kept primarily for display can have different priorities. Discuss how any proposed coating affects appearance, future inspection and maintenance. Photograph the cleaned underside before taking that decision, particularly where you want to preserve a record for the history file.

For a history file, label each pair of photographs with the date, the side of the car and the component shown. A close view of a seam is much easier to interpret when it sits beside a wider image showing its position. Keep a copy of the agreed scope alongside the pictures. Years later, a specialist can then distinguish an area deliberately left untouched from one that was cleaned and subsequently changed. The same record gives a future owner a clear account of the work commissioned and the surfaces that still warrant a closer inspection.

For a consultation at Miracle Detail in Lingfield, provide the model, year, known restoration history and any existing underside photographs from a workshop inspection. Identify the parts that concern you and say whether your goal is preservation, presentation or investigation. The most useful outcome may be a sound original finish revealed, a previously hidden repair documented, or an informed decision to leave a delicate area alone.
